findings.summary: canDrawLogo calls zlib inflateSync on the concatenated IDAT data with no output limit, so a logo of up to 2 MB whose IHDR is within 600 px can inflate to a very large buffer synchronously during export (single-owner upload, so impact is limited to the operator's own machine).
findings.failure_scenario: Owner uploads a crafted PNG with a 600x600 IHDR and a DEFLATE stream that expands to gigabytes; the next GET /api/reports/preview or export allocates that buffer inside canDrawLogo before any drawing starts. Not reproduced here; based on the documented zlib maximum ratio and the code read at lines 177-199.

findings.summary: Outside this unit (reported by the implementer as OBS-c92fa5, not re-verified here): setLogo accepts a PNG with a valid signature/IHDR and corrupt IDAT data, so the file is stored. The export path is protected by canDrawLogo, so no crash was observed in the Done-when suite; the stored logo still fails the export silently and the preview returns it.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner saves a corrupt-IDAT RGBA PNG; PUT /api/brand/logo answers 200; exports fall back to the name-only cover with no message telling the owner why.

findings.summary: Playwright specs tests/e2e/brand.spec.ts and tests/e2e/report.spec.ts were not run: they need the frontend lane (BrandSection, ReportSheet) and a running app; they are capability-level checks, not this unit's Done when.
findings.failure_scenario: Brand upload UI or ReportSheet cover regressions would go unnoticed by this unit's verification.

findings.summary: pnpm build was not run by this review (the implementer reported tests/unit/imageSignature.test.ts, contactFormat.test.ts and tests/api/preferenceRoutes.test.ts passed in the full tests/unit + tests/api run; this review did not re-run that wider suite).
findings.failure_scenario: A build-only break in files outside the Done when would not be caught at unit level.

findings.summary: Play dev-link check (save a PNG and a JPG logo through the running app and export both PDFs) was not run: it needs the Play runtime and a running preview, which this session cannot provide.
findings.failure_scenario: Logo upload through the real runtime and PDF export with a real logo are only covered by the unit/API tests.
